transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’m having trouble explaining things at work. When I try to talk through inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, my words kind of jump around—from trucks to Thursdays to, I don’t know, the church grill or my boss’s tone—and people look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying. It’s been bothering me.
Are you having trouble explaining things or feeling like your words are jumping around in situations outside of work as well?

Yes, it happens outside of work too. If I’m trying to explain something simple, my words can kind of jump around and I lose the thread. It’s like I start with one point, then I’m talking about something else, and people don’t always follow what I mean.
Are these difficulties with explaining things and your words jumping around causing you a lot of distress or significantly impacting your daily life?

Yes. It’s affecting things pretty badly. At work they don’t really trust me to run the busy weekend shifts anymore, and after my last performance review my boss said I could be suspended if I don’t get it together.

At home too, my wife has had to take over things I used to handle, because people get confused or uncomfortable when I’m trying to talk through plans or commitments. It’s embarrassing, and it’s stressful.
Have you been using any alcohol or drugs around the time you notice your words jumping around?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear connection with drinking or drugs. It seems to happen in regular situations too, not like only after I’ve used anything.
Do these episodes of your words jumping around happen all the time, or do they come and go?

It comes and goes. It’s not every single minute, but it happens enough that I notice it. Like when I’m trying to explain inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, I’ll start talking and suddenly I’m jumping from the delivery trucks to Thursday, then something about the church grill, then my boss’s tone. People look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying.
Do you notice any changes in your mood, such as feeling anxious or irritable, when your words are jumping around?

I’m not really sure. I do get frustrated when it happens, because I can tell people aren’t following me, but I haven’t noticed a clear mood change that comes first. It’s more like the stress comes after I realize I’m not making sense.
Do you ever hear or see things that other people don't?

I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t noticed seeing things that aren’t there or hearing voices like that. Sometimes I’m confused in a conversation, but not really hearing or seeing things other people don’t.
Have you ever had a period in your life when you used alcohol or drugs heavily?
No, not that I can think of. I’ve had drinks here and there, but I wouldn’t say there was ever a time I was using alcohol or drugs heavily.
Have you ever had a time when your thoughts seemed completely disconnected from reality?

I don’t know if I’d say completely disconnected from reality. It’s more that when I’m trying to explain something normal, like inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, my words start jumping around. I’ll go from talking about trucks, to Thursday, to some church grill, to my boss’s tone, and then people are looking at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying.
Have you ever had a period where you felt like you were losing touch with reality?

I’m not sure I’d call it losing touch with reality exactly. It’s more like, when I try to explain something at work—inventory numbers or the weekend schedule—my words don’t stay in order. I’ll jump from trucks to Thursday to the church grill to my boss’s tone, and then people just look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying.
Do you feel like your thoughts are jumping around in the same way that your words are when you're trying to explain something?

Yes, I think so. It’s like my thoughts don’t stay in one lane, and then my words come out that way too. I’ll be trying to talk about inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, and suddenly I’m onto trucks, then Thursday, then the church grill, then my boss’s tone. I can tell people are trying to follow me, but they look lost.
Have you noticed a significant change in your ability to perform daily tasks or maintain relationships since your words started jumping around

Yes. It’s affected things pretty clearly. At work, they don’t really trust me to run the busy weekend shifts anymore, and after my last performance review my boss said I could be suspended if I don’t get it together.

At home it’s been hard too. My wife has had to take over commitments I used to handle, because people get uncomfortable or confused when I’m trying to talk things through. It’s embarrassing.
Do you have times when your thoughts and words are completely normal and organized, without any jumping around?

Sometimes, yes, I can sound normal for a while. But when I have to explain something more involved, like inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, that’s when it starts happening. I’ll mean to stay on one point, and then I’m off talking about trucks, Thursdays, the church grill, or my boss’s tone, and people look like they can’t follow me.
Do you feel like your thoughts are as disorganized as your words when you're trying to explain something?

Yes. It feels like it starts in my head first, not just my mouth. I’m trying to explain something simple, like inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, and my thoughts jump from one thing to another — trucks, then Thursday, then the church grill, then something about my boss’s tone. By the time I’m talking, people are looking at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying.
Do you have times when your thoughts and words are completely normal and organized for an entire day, without any jumping around?

Not really for a whole day, no. I can have stretches where I’m fine, but if I have to explain something like the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, it starts jumping around again. I’ll go from trucks to Thursday to the church grill or my boss’s tone, and then people look at me like they’ve lost track of what I’m saying.
Do you have any days where your thoughts and words stay organized and don't jump around at all?

No, I don’t think I get full days where it doesn’t happen at all. I might be okay for a while, but then if I have to explain the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, my words start jumping again — trucks, Thursdays, the church grill, my boss’s tone. Then people look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying.
Do you have any periods of time where your thoughts and words stay organized and don't jump around for several days in a row?

No, I wouldn’t say I get several days in a row where it stays organized. It might be okay for a bit, but then when I try to explain something at work, like the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, it starts jumping around again — trucks, Thursdays, the church grill, my boss’s tone. And then I can see people looking at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying.
Do you have any distinct episodes where your thoughts and words are completely disorganized, or is it more of a constant experience for you?

It feels more constant than like separate episodes. It’s not that I’m fine for days and then suddenly completely disorganized. When I try to explain things, especially at work, like inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, my words start jumping around — trucks, Thursdays, the church grill, my boss’s tone — and people look at me like they can’t follow me.
Do you think your difficulties with explaining things and your words jumping around might be related to your use of alcohol or drugs?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really connected it to alcohol or drugs. I don’t know what you’d be looking for exactly, but I haven’t noticed a clear pattern like that.
Do you think your difficulties with explaining things and your words jumping around started after you began using alcohol or drugs?

I don’t really know. I can’t say it started after alcohol or drugs, because I haven’t noticed a clear before-and-after like that. It’s just been something I’ve had trouble with, especially when I’m trying to explain things.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of disorganized thinking and speech, as evidenced by their words 'jumping around' when trying to explain things, are consistent with a diagnosis of Schizophrenia, unspecified (F23). The patient's difficulties with explaining things, feeling embarrassed and stressed, and experiencing functional impairment at work and home support this diagnosis. The patient's denial of substance use as a contributing factor and lack of clear evidence of substance-induced psychosis reduce the likelihood of a diagnosis related to substance use (F10.1). The patient's symptoms do not appear to be solely related to a speech or language disorder (R47.0), as they report difficulties with thinking and organizing their thoughts, not just speaking.
